name: Lustre painting
summary: A paint with copper and silver salts is brushed on a glazed pot. A second firing in a smoky kiln leaves a thin layer of metal with a gold or copper shine.
how: Fire the pot with a tin glaze and let it cool.
Paint the pattern with a mix of copper or silver salts, ochre and vinegar.
Fire the pot again at about 600 °C in a smoky kiln.
Wash off the ochre to show the metallic film.

origin.note: Abbasid potters make the first lustre on glazed pots.

adoptions.via: Abbasid potters paint bowls and tiles with lustre in brown, gold and olive.
Moorish potters in Malaga and Valencia bring lustre to Spain and make it a trade ware.
